newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed down across the board in dull trading on Thursday mainly due to a plunge on the falls on the A share markets in the past two days, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded three-day contract fell to 5.00 percent from 8.01 percent on Wednesday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market plunged to 1.8 million lots from 3.8 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Share prices on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges plunged in the past two days partly due to rumours of fresh offical measures to cool down stock trading, traders said.
Traders said the plunge greatly weakened sentiment on the repo market, which has served as a money reservoir for the stock markets.
"Fund demand fell sharply with institutions reluctant to build positions," one trader said. "This led the repo rates to fall with volumes also falling sharply."
Traders said they expected the rates to fall further, but only slightly, on Friday.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended up across the board on Thursday with investors moving money to the spot market due to the stock market falls, traders said.
The most actively traded three-year bond that matures in August 1999 rose to 108.44 yuan from 108.00 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose sharply to 785,669 lots from 494,869 lots.
Traders said sentiment on the spot market had become a little better with fresh liquidity flowing in.
They said they expected the spot contracts to rise further on Friday on the back of the weak stock markets.
